title: Credential-access toolchain staged and executed from user-writable paths (SysinternalsSuite, psversion.ps1, accesschk, sdelete, PsExec)
rationale: Same staging/execution of credential-access tooling (SysinternalsSuite download/unpack, accesschk, sdelete64, PsExec64) on scranton and nashua; general OS credential dumping tooling, best fit T1003.

title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by attacker PowerShell on scranton and wsmprovhost on nashua
rationale: All describe the same LSASS handle-open events: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton opening lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff and UNKNOWN call trace, and wsmprovhost.exe on nashua with 0x1f3fff. This is LSASS memory access, best fit T1003.001.

title: LSA registry key read by pbeesly's processes on scranton
rationale: 4663/4673 events on HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Lsa consistent with LSA secrets access; best fit T1003.004.

title: PowerShell screen capture and clipboard harvesting on scranton
rationale: Invoke-ScreenCapture and Get-Clipboard in pbeesly's PowerShell session; GUI input capture, best fit T1056.002.

title: No brute-force authentication attempts observed
rationale: Finding explicitly assesses brute force as not observed; the only credential-access signal is LSASS access. Retained under T1110 as the technique it evaluated.

title: No password-cracking tooling or hash files found
rationale: Finding evaluates password cracking and finds no cracking artifacts; only LSASS handle access stands out. Retained under T1110.002 as the technique it evaluated.

title: Hardcoded plaintext credentials in attacker tooling on scranton
rationale: Same embedded plaintext credentials (saribas, cozy/MyCozyPassw0rd!, Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by) in tooling; unsecured credentials, best fit T1552.

title: Credential-bearing files staged and archived on scranton and nashua
rationale: Same passwordsDB, Draft.Zip, OfficeSupplies.7z and working.zip collection/archiving events; credentials in files, best fit T1552.001.

title: Private key and certificate export to password-protected .pfx on scranton
rationale: Same Get-PrivateKeys action exporting LocalMachine certificates/private keys to a .pfx in Downloads; best fit T1552.004.

title: PowerShell opens LSASS with full access on scranton and nashua (credential store access)
rationale: F65 (hostui.exe reading Explorer memory) and F66/F67 (malicious .scr execution and sdclt UAC-bypass burst) are grouped here as the surrounding credential-store/UI-harvesting activity; best fit T1555 for the credential-store access context.

title: Credential theft and lateral movement by pbeesly; no authentication-process modification
rationale: Finding evaluates authentication-process modification and finds none; the observed action is credential theft plus lateral movement. Retained under T1556 as the technique it evaluated.

title: No hybrid-identity backdoor; service installs are PsExec/Java
rationale: Finding evaluates hybrid identity modification and finds only PSEXESVC and Java service installs. Retained under T1556.007 as the technique it evaluated.

title: No web cookie theft/forging; malicious .scr execution and PsExec with plaintext password
rationale: Finding evaluates web cookie forging and finds none; observed activity is execution and lateral movement. Retained under T1606.001 as the technique it evaluated.

title: Persistent RSA machine key exported and written to .pfx on scranton
rationale: Security 5058/5059 key read and export by pbeesly's PowerShell producing a .pfx; steal or forge authentication certificates, best fit T1649.

title: hostui.exe persistence and registry-stored base64 PowerShell stager on scranton
rationale: Startup .lnk and HKLM registry base64 stager with hostui.bat execution is persistence/execution, not credential access.
